title: VEL-VIV-CELEB-GS-01 - Katie x Sofia quiet luxury (greenscreen)

cards.text: VEL-VIV-CELEB-GS-01 - KATIE X SOFIA QUIET LUXURY (GREENSCREEN)

cards.title: CONCEPT
cards.text: BUILT 2026-08-31 - three finished ads, creator-only A/B/C, 58.5s each, 1080x1920. The Vivienne sold the way the reference sells Brad Pitt: the celebrity is the MECHANISM, not decoration. It never claims either woman carries ours - it claims the LOOK is theirs, prices that look at ten thousand dollars, then hands over the affordable route. Combo hook: Katie still, Sofia still, 4.6s total, then we are on our bag for the rest of the ad. Timecodes below are the REAL ones, taken from the voiceover's own word alignment, not estimates.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Okay, so if you love that Katie Holmes,
STILL, hard hold, zero camera move. Katie Holmes on the tarmac, chocolate top-handle in her hand.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: recognition - HOOK. She stops the scroll because she already knows this woman and already wants this bag.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Sofia Richie energy,
STILL, hard hold. Sofia Richie in the rain, oxblood top-handle in her hand.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: confirmation - HOOK PART 2. Two names makes it a pattern, not a coincidence. The look has a category now.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: always in a Birkin shape bag, never a logo,
Our chocolate Vivienne on an unmade bed. Full trapezoid, clean front.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: quiet recognition - THE BRIDGE. Same shape, our bag, no announcement. Katie's bag was chocolate too and we never say so.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: quiet luxury written all over it, you already know the problem.
Shoulder strap, walking away down a hallway, bag moulding against her hip.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: aspiration turning to friction - PROBLEM SET-UP. 'You already know the problem' names the objection before she can.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Every bag that gives you that look
Back to Sofia's still with the burned $10,000+ card over it.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: sticker shock - THE GUT PUNCH. The card does the work; the VO never names a house.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: starts around ten thousand dollars.
HARD CUT to our bag on a kitchen counter next to keys, a mug and a receipt.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: relief - THE ARGUMENT IS THE CUT. Ten-thousand-dollar object, then the same shape lying by a receipt.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: So I hunted down the affordable version.
Hand reaches in and grabs it off the entryway bench.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: discovery - SHE FOUND IT, not the brand. The creator is the finder, that is the whole trust mechanic.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: It's called the Vivienne by Velantra.
Hung over a chair back under a single table lamp. The beauty frame.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: arrival - PRODUCT INTRO. The name lands over the most flattering frame in the library.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Same silhouette, no logo, actually accessible.
Riding on the passenger seat, daylight through the glass.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: permission - THE POSITIONING LINE. 'Actually accessible' is the promise the offer will pay off.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: It's vegetable tanned leather all the way through,
Fingers press flat into the front panel, natural pore grain, matte to satin.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: material trust - ATTRIBUTE 1. Touch proves hide. The press is the claim.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: with an aged brass belted turn lock,
Fingers turning the brass lock closed, macro.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
craft - ATTRIBUTE 2. Mechanism demonstrated, not described.

The only cut where a mechanism actually moves. Let it complete.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: braided leather trim,
Braided whip-stitch trim along the band, overhead macro.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
detail - ATTRIBUTE 3. The thing a cheap bag cannot fake.

Shortest cut in the ad. Snap in, snap out.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: and zero branding anywhere on it.
The whole clean front panel lifted into the light, bare leather, hand clear of frame.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
quiet superiority - ATTRIBUTE 4 and the brand's thesis. The absence IS the feature.

SHIPPED THE FALLBACK, not the GAP-02 macro - see the note on the board.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: It's soft, so instead of sitting stiff on your arm
The bag collapsed into the duvet, sides folded, holding no shape at all.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
reassurance - THE DIFFERENTIATOR OPENS. Every bag in this shape is rigid. Ours is not.

Replaces the storyboard's second press frame, which twinned with 0:27.7 when built.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: like most bags in this shape,
Handles released, the bag drops and settles.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
contrast - THE DISMISSAL. The stiff-bag insult is spoken over OUR bag doing the opposite.

Never cut to a competitor bag for a dismissal. The slump is the rebuttal.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: it slouches and molds to you as you carry it.
On the hip, walking, body moulding to her as she moves.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text: ownership - SHE CAN SEE HERSELF CARRYING IT. Last emotional beat before the offer.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: And right now they've actually just opened pre orders on it.
Walking out the front door, bag in hand, blown daylight ahead.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
forward motion - THE TURN INTO THE OFFER.

Last piece of b-roll. Everything after this is the website.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Twenty five percent off, one forty nine instead of one ninety nine, and the first run ships in October. I've left the link below.
Live PDP screen recording. ONE unbroken scroll: price and swatches, Add to Cart, then the October pre-order paragraph, which settles and HOLDS.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
decision - OFFER AND CTA. The ad ends on the website and never cuts back to the bag.

No cuts inside this.

cards.title: VEL-VIV-CELEB-GS-01 - as built  ·  58.5s, 18 cuts, avg 3.25s - one shared VO, three creators

cards.text: NOTES

cards.title: THREE FINISHED ADS - A / B / C
cards.text: Diane 58, Bridget 53, Marguerite 62. One shared voiceover drives all three, so the bed, the captions and every timing are identical and ONLY the creator changes - a clean creator-only test. Shipped with the words 'clean girl' cut from the hook, so the line reads 'that Katie Holmes, Sofia Richie energy' and a 62 year old is not saying 'clean girl'. Say the word and a fresh 35-45 trio is a re-render on the same VO.

cards.title: PiP REBUILT - the creator is now CUT BY THE FRAME EDGE
cards.text: v1 had her floating in the corner as a complete cutout with air around her whole silhouette - a sticker pasted on the b-roll. The bug was sizing the PiP on the PLATE (the inherited '32% of frame width' rule) when our creator keyframes were generated wide and waist-up, so her head came out tiny and her full outline showed. Measured off the shipped GS-BIRKIN-01 and BLK-01 ads instead: the house sizes on the HEAD (~20% of frame width, top at ~y1300) and lets the frame crop her on TWO edges. She now runs 60px below the bottom and 64-73px past the near side. Captions moved from y1330 to y1120 to clear her head.

cards.title: RUNTIME MOVED: 46.5s -> 58.5s
cards.text: The storyboard estimate assumed 180 wpm. This read came back at ~152. Nothing was cut and nothing was sped up - the one-take and no-atempo laws both say the read ships as-is, so the bed stretched to fit her. Average cut is 3.25s, inside the range GS-BIRKIN-01 shipped at.

cards.title: GAP-02 WAS NOT GENERATED - THE FALLBACK SHIPPED
cards.text: The seed the spec called for is the real unboxing frame, and it carries an ATORIE hang tag and the source listing's hardware, not ours. Seeding a 'zero branding anywhere on it' macro from a frame with a brand tag in it is the wrong move, and every other real frame has the same problem. 0:34.8 is the approved fallback instead: the clean front panel lifted into the light, hand clear. If you want the dedicated macro it needs a clean-room generation off the identity block, not an i2i - a separate job.

cards.title: FIXED DURING THE BUILD
cards.text: Three things the storyboard could not have known. (1) 0:37.4 was a second copy of the press-the-leather clip and twinned badly once built - it is now the bag collapsed into the duvet, a better frame for that line anyway. (2) The caption builder was merging short cards across sentence ends and produced one EIGHT-SECOND card spanning two cuts; it now breaks sentence to phrase to card and caps at 2.9s. (3) Cards sat at y=1500 and collided with the keyed creator's head, and had no scrim over the white PDP - they now sit at y=1330 with a feathered scrim measured on each line's own ink.

cards.title: STILL OPEN FOR YOU
cards.text: 1. The first-run scarcity line is still NOT in the ad. The '50,000 waitlist' and 'sold out seven times' were the reference ad's fabricated numbers. If it is true that the price returns to $199.99 after the first run, that line goes in and the VO re-renders. 2. Both hook frames are unlicensed press photography of real people. The ad never claims either carries ours, but it is worth your eyes before Meta review.

cards.title: DON'T
cards.text: Do not cut to a competitor bag for the 'most bags in this shape' dismissal - the insult is spoken over OUR bag doing the opposite. Do not put 'Birkin' in any generation prompt, ever; it lives in VO and captions only. Do not use the cafe-floor clip - she would not set a leather bag on a cafe floor. Do not cut back to the bag after the website.
